source.title: Are Sparse Autoencoders Useful? A Case Study in Sparse Probing
source.authors: Subhash Kantamneni; Joshua Engels; Senthooran Rajamanoharan; Max Tegmark; Neel Nanda

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling, truncation, or document mismatch; the paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates SAE-latent probing on LLM activations as a different-method test of whether dictionaries recover task-relevant features. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper's main comparisons of SAE probes with ordinary probes, plus its task-specific latent AUC results, bear on whether SAE dictionaries recover task-relevant features in LLMs (V4). Results about L0, k, layer choice, and architecture selection are included only where reported as outcomes, not as evidence for superposition geometry. The many per-dataset values in Table 9 and several supplementary figures are not all reproduced here; see rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: The main result, SAE probes against strong baselines, measures downstream probing utility. That is a related but different construct from whether SAEs recover the model's features, so it goes under fits_no_version. Two results do bear on the claim. Single-latent AUCs show that individual SAE latents capture task concepts in Gemma-2-9B (indirect evidence for V4). The English-only 'living room' latent and the mislabelled or spurious latents bear on whether SAE latents are stable, complete concept units (V5). No toy-model, capacity, polysemanticity or dimensionality tests appear.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is largely correct. Add three points. Simple baselines reproduced most of the interpretability insights (spurious correlations, CoLA mislabelling). The authors attribute OOD failure to SAE latents not generalizing, quoting 'fail to represent complex concepts'. They stress that probing is only a proxy for SAE utility.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates supervised probes on SAE latents in LLMs rather than testing the original toy-model superposition setup or measuring overlapping feature directions.
record.method_sensitivity: Probe outcomes vary with task dataset and distribution shift; SAE L0 and number of selected latents k affect probe performance; latent 122774 is language-sensitive; architecture comparisons show a slight but non-significant trend.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding SAE probes to a baseline toolkit gives no average AUC gain. This holds in standard, scarce-data, imbalanced, noisy and shifted regimes on Gemma-2-9B and Llama-3.1-8B. Newer SAE architectures and binarization do not change this meaningfully.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents provide a downstream probing advantage over strong non-SAE baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: Pruning latents judged spurious by o1 gives small OOD gains on 2 of 3 tasks. The gains are much smaller than the ID-to-OOD drop.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spurious latents explain SAE-probe OOD failure.

record.code_released: The paper says its code is publicly available, but no URL is stated in the supplied text.
record.problems: The paper treats probing performance as a proxy for SAE utility rather than comparing features with ground truth. Several plotted comparisons are not given numerically in the text. The OOD tests cover a limited set of 8 datasets, and some examples show that task prediction may reflect spurious dataset correlations.
record.rows_left_out: The per-dataset and per-method values in Table 9, additional individual-dataset curves in Figures 15–19 and 21, and the full latent ranking values in Table 5 are not separately cataloged. They contain many more condition-level results than can be usefully represented here; the principal aggregate outcomes and selected individual latent results are recorded above.

untested.parts: All: no toy networks, geometry or sparsity transition.
All: no capacity or importance analysis of neurons.
All: polysemantic neurons are not studied.
Spread of features across neurons. Recovery against ground truth: the authors note none exists. Rates over all latents rather than curated examples.
Canonicity across SAEs or seeds; completeness of the dictionary overall.
All: no comparison of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

missing.what: Latent 122774 activation across 15 translations of 'living room': highest on English, zero on French
Validation ID and OOD test AUC for the other seven living-room latents, e.g. 51330 with OOD AUC 0.6483 (highest) despite an unrelated description

record.verdict_notes: The record over-links: utility comparisons are not tests of whether SAEs recover features, so only single-latent results are kept on V4. The Table 6 single-latent rows are a curated selection and should not be read as rates. Table 6 category boundaries are hard to read in the extracted text. The text's 'increases by 0.077' for ispolitician pruning contradicts its own statement that pruning failed there.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether neuron polysemanticity results from limited capacity or features competing for dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The study measures task-label prediction from SAE latents, not feature spread across neurons, nor recovery against ground-truth model features.
It does not establish whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of model representations.
It does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

rows.note: The authors describe a slight decrease; SAE probes were selected for 14/113 tasks.

relation.reason: The study reports its own measurements of concept prediction by individual dictionary latents, bearing on V4.

tranche.reason: Selected single-latent results provide indirect evidence of dictionary recoverability using a different method from the original toy experiment. The main comparison of probing methods measures downstream utility.

reader_labels.condition: Distribution shift, spurious label correlations, and aggregate probe comparisons
reader_labels.reason: SAE probe gains are absent or limited in the reported aggregate comparisons; latent task prediction can rely on spurious cues and can fall sharply under shift, as in r1-r5, r7-r8, r23-r25, r27, and r35.
